title: Yosano Akiko's birth chart
metaDescription: Yosano Akiko's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.9° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 14.1° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 14.9° Sagittarius. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Mars in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a mutable season.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Capricorn (5.6°), Venus in Sagittarius (15.2°), Mars in Scorpio (18.1°): a mind that trusts the measured and the checked, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun to Venus is the closest call of the day, a conjunction within 0.3°. The tradition stops reading a conjunction as two things. It is one appetite with two names, and it moves together or not at all. Behind it, Saturn sextile Pluto at 1.1°, and Mercury trine Uranus at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mercury, Uranus, Neptune close a triangle of trines. A grand trine is read as self-sufficiency in one element: the current circulates whether or not anything is asked of it.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. The Moon in Taurus at 14.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Scorpio at 18.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives earth 5, fire 2, water 2, air 1, and fixed 5, mutable 4, cardinal 1 across the modes. An earth emphasis reads as trust in the tangible: the plan matters less than whether the thing stands up. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.1° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 14.1°.
